Growatt VPP Integration Architecture
Executive Summary

One architecture, three integration paths

Cloud-to-Cloud

Standard VPP and fleet integration through Growatt Unified Open API.

  • Best for residential fleet scale
  • TOU, dynamic price, DR
  • Cloud optimization + edge execution

Cloud-to-Edge

Partner cloud connects directly to local gateway or edge EMS.

  • C&I, parallel systems
  • Site-level EMS
  • Higher real-time dispatch

Edge-to-Edge

Local controller connects to Growatt edge for real-time local control.

  • FCR / FFR
  • Microgrid
  • Local closed-loop control

The higher the real-time requirement, the lower the control loop should move.

Protocol Boundary

Device protocol standardizes devices; system protocol standardizes sites

Device Unified RTU Protocol

Single-device abstraction for inverter, battery, meter, PCS or PV inverter.

  • Device telemetry and status
  • Alarm and fault codes
  • Device-level control and configuration
  • Firmware-dependent capability

System Unified RTU Protocol

Site-level aggregation for multiple devices, parallel systems and heterogeneous topologies.

  • Site energy flow
  • Aggregated SOC and available power
  • Site-level control points
  • Topology, meter and health status

WIT PCS

Role: PCS for C&I BESS and parallel systems.

  • Meter / PCC closed-loop control
  • System-level capability envelope

Architecture implication

For C&I products such as RISE All-in-One and WIT PCS, the preferred integration path is Edge-to-Edge using System Unified RTU / Edge EMS API. Device RTU secured pass-through remains valid for single-device systems, but site-level systems require topology, metering, capability and control-point abstraction.

Unified Open API capability view
Safety-first Design

Safety and local fail-safe control hierarchy

Local safety has the highest priority

Device-level safety is always handled locally and cannot be overridden by cloud or VPP commands.

  • Battery BMS protection
  • Inverter grid protection
  • Thermal derating and fault lockout
  • Anti-islanding and grid code protection

Export limit is locally executed

The cloud or VPP may send the target. The local gateway, EMS or device controller enforces it locally.

  • Local execution at site
  • Local fallback on communication loss
  • Optional forced export-limit = 0
  • Meter / PCC validity required

Safety overrides dispatch. Local fail-safe overrides cloud optimization. BMS protection overrides all external control.

Partner-facing value proposition
Final Takeaway

Recommended external positioning

Growatt supports flexible VPP integration across cloud, edge and device layers. Partners can choose Cloud-to-Cloud for scale, Cloud-to-Edge for site-level control, and Edge-to-Edge for high real-time grid services.

Architecture principle

Cloud = semantic model, optimization, API and fleet operation Edge = local execution, aggregation, fail-safe and real-time control Device = physical response and intrinsic safety

Key statement

Cloud-to-Cloud solves scale. Cloud-to-Edge solves site control. Edge-to-Edge solves high real-time response: - Device RTU secured pass-through for single-device systems - System RTU / Edge EMS for site-level systems such as RISE / WIT Safety remains local and has the highest priority.
